items.reviewedFinding: After et and a preceding numbered noun, demi is a singular adjective agreeing in gender and expressing half that unit; the noun-half use is listed separately.
The figurative deceiving or catching-out use is distinct from physical trapping, capture of a person and attraper froid.
An old coin commonly of gold and sometimes silver, varying by place; no fixed price or purity is inferred.
Records the proposed principle of life and, for humans, thought and voluntary movement; this explains historical philosophical language without establishing the principle as a scientific fact.
Records the essential form constituting an individual and directing an organized being toward its ends; philosophers disagree about the term.
Records completed actuality as distinct from an act in progress, with realized essence in Leibniz; compare rather than equate it with mere potentiality.
The masculine noun denotes an adherent of Aristotle’s philosophy, with adjective usage separately marked.
The idiom denotes speaking or making an address in an assembly; it is not literally grasping the noun parole.
Records the non-pronominal discussion construction, arguing questions on opposing sides, including sur a proposition.

Preposed adjectives with a distinct feminine form agree feminine; this agreement is not extended to other sentence elements except tout and quel. The stored middle bank has no gender-selecting adjective.
Lists vieux and vieille as substantive nouns as well as adjectives; relative age alone does not license duplicate old/oldest meanings.

Cause, motive and explanatory ground are distinct from the faculty of reason and being right. Applying explanatory-ground scope to the speaker’s sentence is an editorial inference, not verification of his alleged Aristotle quotation.
